translationRepairs: When An Lushan rebelled, Suzong pursued him; when the edict arrived, [Siye] immediately led the way, and with the generals cut their arms in covenant, saying: "In every commandery and county we pass, not a hair's breadth may be violated."

When An Lushan rebelled, Suzong summoned him; when the edict arrived, [Siye] immediately led the way, and with the generals cut their arms in covenant, saying: "In every commandery and county we pass, not a hair's breadth may be violated."
肅宗追之 refers to recalling Siye; the following 詔至 and audience at Fengxiang show summons, not pursuit of An Lushan.
He then joined Zhang Hao, Lu Jiong, Lai Tian, the Prince of Wu Zhi, and Li Huan in broadly pacifying the various prefectures.
He then joined Zhang Hao, Lu Jiong, Lai Tian, Zhi the Successor Prince of Wu, and Li Huan in broadly pacifying the various prefectures.
嗣吳王祗 is the title 嗣吳王 plus the personal name 祗; 'the Prince of Wu Zhi' wrongly folds Zhi into the title.
遂戮之 continues Lin as agent with 之 as the thief; 'He was then executed' wrongly makes Lin the executee.
Lin had studied the classics in youth, yet his martial gifts were without peer.
Lin had little scholarly learning, yet his martial gifts were without peer.
少學術 means deficient in learning; contrasted with 武幹絕倫 it cannot mean youthful classical study.
Lin studied the classics in youth, yet his martial talent was without peer.
Lin had little scholarship, yet his martial talent was without peer.
Same 少學術 error in the literal: lack of scholarship, not study of the classics in youth.
He was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Martial.
He was posthumously made Minister over the Masses with the posthumous name Martial.
贈司徒 is the Three Dukes office 司徒, not Grand Tutor 太傅.
He was posthumously made Grand Tutor; his posthumous title was Martial.
He was posthumously made Minister over the Masses; his posthumous title was Martial.
Literal likewise misrenders 司徒 as Grand Tutor; Minister over the Masses is correct.
He earnestly declined the princely title and was made Duke of Liang, then promoted to Grand Tutor.
He earnestly declined the princely title and was made Duke of Liang, then promoted to Minister over the Masses.
進司徒 advances him to 司徒, not Grand Tutor 太傅.
He earnestly declined the princely title and was transferred to Duke of Liang, then advanced to Grand Tutor.
He earnestly declined the princely title and was transferred to Duke of Liang, then advanced to Minister over the Masses.
Literal likewise misrenders 進司徒 as advancement to Grand Tutor.
Late in the Tianbao era the emperor renamed him for his merit fighting in Hexi.
Late in the Tianbao era Xuanzong renamed him for his merit fighting in Hexi.
Chinese names 玄宗; replacing that temple name with a generic 'the emperor' drops the specified identity.
The bandit leader Gao Yu fled to Chenggu; Zhang Xianzheng of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan captured him and sent him in; all his followers were hunted down and executed.
The bandit leader Gao Yu fled to Chenggu; Zhang Xiancheng of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan captured him and sent him in; all his followers were hunted down and executed.
張獻誠 uses 誠 (chéng); Xianzheng invents a wrong given-name reading.
The bandit chief Gao Yu escaped to Chenggu; Zhang Xianzheng of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan captured and presented him; all associates were sought out and beheaded.
The bandit chief Gao Yu escaped to Chenggu; Zhang Xiancheng of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan captured and presented him; all associates were sought out and beheaded.
Literal has the same 誠/政 romanization error; Xiancheng restores the graph.
Before long he was also made Deputy Commander and Military Commissioner of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan, with headquarters at Ziwu.
Before long he was also made Deputy Commander and Military Commissioner of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan, with headquarters at Zhouzhi.
Local 鷫厔 is a graphic variant of 盩厔 (Zhouzhi); ZZTJ records Baoyu moving his garrison to 盩厔, not Ziwu.
After long he was given the additional titles of Deputy Commander and Military Commissioner of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan, and encamped at Ziwu.
After long he was given the additional titles of Deputy Commander and Military Commissioner of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan, and encamped at Zhouzhi.
Literal likewise misreads 鷫厔/盩厔 as Ziwu; Zhouzhi matches the historical place name.
Huai'en has deceived his men, telling them that Ziyi was killed by court intrigue.
Huai'en has deceived his men, telling them that Ziyi was killed by Chao'en.
朝恩 is the personal name Chao'en, not an abstract 'court intrigue'.
Huai'en deceived his subordinates, saying, 'Ziyi was killed by court favoritism.
Huai'en deceived his subordinates, saying, 'Ziyi was killed by Chao'en.
Literal likewise invents 'court favoritism' for the personal name 朝恩.
Lu Sigong, courtesy name Yifan, came from Sanyuan in Jingzhao. Born Jiank, he entered office through hereditary privilege as adjutant of Ye.
Lu Sigong, courtesy name Yifan, came from Sanyuan in Jingzhao. Originally named Jianke, he entered office through hereditary privilege as adjutant of Ye.
始名劍客 is Jianke; truncating to Jiank and the awkward 'Born Jiank' corrupt the name.
Lu Sigong, courtesy name Yifan, a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao; his original name was Jiank; through hereditary privilege he became Commandery Adjutant of Ye.
Lu Sigong, courtesy name Yifan, a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao; his original name was Jianke; through hereditary privilege he became Commandery Adjutant of Ye.
Literal likewise corrupts 劍客 to Jiank; Jianke restores the full reading.

Baozhen's son Jian, a palace attendant, concealed his father's death. With his subordinates Lu Huichang and Yuan Zhongjing he assembled the generals; Zhongjing forged an order in Baozhen's name: "My illness prevents me from governing. Jian shall command the army—assist him faithfully."

Baozhen's son Jian, a Palace Attendant Censor, concealed his father's death. With his subordinates Lu Huichang and Yuan Zhongjing he assembled the generals; Zhongjing forged an order in Baozhen's name: "My illness prevents me from governing. Jian shall command the army—assist him faithfully."
殿中侍御史 is the censorate office Palace Attendant Censor, not a vague palace attendant.
Wei Shaoyou, fearing Zai, had long indulged Jia. When Sigong replaced him, he had Jia beaten to death that same day.
Wei Shaoyou, fearing Zai, had long indulged Jia. When Sigong replaced Shaoyou, he had Jia beaten to death that same day.
Chinese 代少遊 names Shaoyou; with Zai and Jia also in view, bare 'him' drops that explicit referent.
Once I rode alongside his son Ying when a horse bit my shin. I was terrified, but Ying said nothing and went calmly to see his father.
Once I rode alongside his son Ying when a horse bit my shin. I was terrified, but Ying said nothing and forced himself up to see his father.
勉起見父 means he forced himself up to see his father; 'went calmly' invents composure absent from the Chinese.
He later served as observation commissioner of Bin-Fang and of Xuan-She.
He later served as observation commissioner of Fu-Fang and of Xuan-She.
鄜坊 is Fu and Fang; Bin (邠) is a different circuit, so Bin-Fang mistranslates 鄜.
His son Ying, courtesy name Congzhong, entered office by privilege as a drafting secretary.
His son Ying, courtesy name Congzhong, entered office by privilege as a Gentleman Compiler.
著作郎 is Gentleman Compiler; 'drafting secretary' misidentifies the office.
